summary: The existing service is a single minimal-API project with a thin domain layer and EF Core SQLite persistence. Analytics can be added without touching the create/get/delete paths: the redirect handler becomes the only producer of click events, a new ClickEvent entity joins the model, a bounded queue plus background writer decouples persistence from the request, and one new read endpoint aggregates.
architecture: Composition root in Program.cs -> Endpoints/LinkEndpoints (HTTP) -> Domain (ShortLink, ShortCodeGenerator, UrlValidator) -> Data/AppDbContext (EF Core, SQLite). Tests boot the real pipeline via ApiFactory (WebApplicationFactory) with one SQLite file per test class.

impactedModules.reason: RedirectAsync must enqueue a click; a new GetStatsAsync handler and route are needed.
Add DbSet<ClickEvent>, index on (LinkId, OccurredAtUtc), cascade delete from ShortLink.
Register ClickQueue singleton and ClickRecorder hosted service.
New bounded channel between redirect and writer.
New BackgroundService that batches writes and drains on shutdown.
New integration tests for recording and aggregation.

dataFlows: GET /{code} -> AppDbContext.Links lookup -> ClickQueue.TryEnqueue(ClickEvent) -> 302 (unchanged latency profile)
ClickRecorder (background) -> ClickQueue.Reader -> batch of <=100 -> AppDbContext.Clicks.AddRange -> SaveChanges (retry on SQLite busy)
GET /api/links/{code}/stats -> Links lookup -> Clicks aggregate (count, max, last-7-days projection) -> LinkStatsResponse
DELETE /api/links/{code} -> cascade removes ClickEvents (FK with Cascade)
testsAffected: New StatsApiTests: async recording, aggregation shape, unknown link 404, redirect latency independent of writes.
risks: SQLite 'database is locked' under concurrent writers: the background writer must retry with backoff.
DateTimeOffset columns cannot be compared/aggregated by the SQLite EF provider: ClickEvent must store a UTC DateTime.
Unbounded queue growth under load: queue must be bounded with an explicit drop policy.
Schema change (new table) with EnsureCreated: existing databases created by v1.0 will NOT get the new table automatically - migrations or a fresh database are required.
recommendedApproach: Additive change: new entity + two new analytics classes + one new endpoint; modify only the redirect handler, the DbContext, Program registration and the DTO file. Keep every existing test green and verify redirect latency independence with a test.
